questions.markdown: Explain a dangling pointer and a memory leak using one short C example of each. State how each error can be prevented.
reviewNotes: AI generated questions and worked solutions, typeset in the Manipal practice format. Computational checks cover applicable answers.
questions.preparedSolution:
A dangling pointer refers to storage whose lifetime has ended:

    int *p = malloc(sizeof *p);
    free(p);       /* p now dangles; do not dereference it. */
    p = NULL;      /* Clear this pointer after releasing storage. */

Any aliases must also stop using that storage. A memory leak loses the final reference to allocated storage:

    int *p = malloc(sizeof *p);
    p = NULL;      /* Wrong: allocated storage can no longer be freed. */

Keep an owning pointer and free the allocation before overwriting that final reference. These examples illustrate errors; they are not code to copy into a working implementation.

questions.markdown: A list initially contains $10\to20\to30$. Insert 5 at the head, insert 25 after 20, then delete the tail. Draw the final list and state how many next links must be traversed to locate its tail from the head.
reviewNotes: AI generated questions and worked solutions, typeset in the Manipal practice format. Computational checks cover applicable answers.
questions.preparedSolution:
``` math
10\to20\to30
\quad\longrightarrow\quad5\to10\to20\to30
```
``` math
\longrightarrow\quad5\to10\to20\to25\to30
\quad\longrightarrow\quad\boxed{5\to10\to20\to25}.
```
Starting at the final head, follow three next links to reach tail 25. Checking that the tail’s next pointer is NULL does not traverse another node-to-node link.

questions.markdown: Convert `A+B*(C-D)^E^F` to postfix using a stack. Exponentiation has highest precedence and is right-associative. Show the operator stack and output after each input token, then give the final postfix expression.
reviewNotes: AI generated questions and worked solutions, typeset in the Manipal practice format. Computational checks cover applicable answers.
questions.preparedSolution:
The stack is listed bottom to top. Exponentiation is right-associative, so the second exponentiation does not pop the first.



| Token      | Operator stack           | Output        |
|:-----------|:-------------------------|:--------------|
| A          | empty                    | A             |
| \+         | \+                       | A             |
| B          | \+                       | AB            |
| \*         | \+ \*                    | AB            |
| (          | \+ \* (                  | AB            |
| C          | \+ \* (                  | ABC           |
| \-         | \+ \* ( -                | ABC           |
| D          | \+ \* ( -                | ABCD          |
| )          | \+ \*                    | ABCD-         |
| $\wedge$ | $+\ *\ \wedge$         | ABCD-         |
| E          | $+\ *\ \wedge$         | ABCD-E        |
| $\wedge$ | $+\ *\ \wedge\ \wedge$ | ABCD-E        |
| F          | $+\ *\ \wedge\ \wedge$ | ABCD-EF       |
| End        | empty                    | `ABCD-EF^^*+` |



Thus the final postfix form is . The two exponentiations encode $(C-D)^{(E^F)}$.

questions.markdown: An editor uses undo and redo stacks. Starting with empty stacks, perform edits A, B and C, then undo twice and redo once. List both stacks from bottom to top. State what happens to the redo stack when a new edit D is made.
reviewNotes: AI generated questions and worked solutions, typeset in the Manipal practice format. Computational checks cover applicable answers.
questions.preparedSolution:
| Operation     | Undo: bottom to top | Redo: bottom to top |
|:--------------|:--------------------|:--------------------|
| Edits A, B, C | A, B, C             | empty               |
| Undo          | A, B                | C                   |
| Undo          | A                   | C, B                |
| Redo          | A, B                | C                   |
| New edit D    | A, B, D             | empty               |



Undo transfers the newest applied action to redo; redo reapplies its newest undone action. New edit D clears redo, since C belongs to the abandoned editing branch.
